page.layout: Two printed pages on the scan. Left page: one column of running text with Greek, Hebrew and italic glosses, page number 406 at the head, running head Σ I. Right page: narrow marginal notes down the right edge, cut off at the scan edge. Lines of the margin are notes, transcribed as far as legible.

main_text.p: Σιδήρε῾ο ᾱς, ἐη ἡ, (᾿Doricè ἐα ᾱ) ἐον ἂν, Act. 12. 10. πύλῃ σιδηρᾷ porta ferrea. vide ᾿Ἀγῳ- ρς῾ supra.
Σικάριος ὁ vox origine Latina, ficarius à fica quasi feca, est gladiolus. Graece μά- λων ὠν῾ ὁ ein Dolch pugio sic dictus à pungendo.

Σίκερα τὸ ἀκλίτον ficera, per quam intelligitur potus quilibet inebrians, praeter vinum. prout apud nos sunt potus factitii, cerevisia, quas Tacitus vina vocat hordeacea. vox hac est origine Hebraica שכר.
Σίναπι ἑως τὸ sinápi, τὸ σίνεσ τῆς ὤπως, quod eo ladantur oculi.
Σινδὼν ὁν῾ ὁ sindon, sindonis. Heb. סדין sadin, est linum tenue & pretiosum. Martialis vocat Tyriam sindonem.

Σινάζω ventilo, vanno vel crybro perpurgo. F. ἀσω. P. σεσινιάκα. a.1. ἐσινιάσα. aor.1. act. infin. σινιάσαι, Luc.22.31. idem quod κοσκινίζω à κόσκινον & τὸ cribrum. videtur derivari à σείω concutio. Hesych.
Σίλιβτος ἡ ὀν faginatus a um. à verbo σιλβώ frugibus fagino ich messe mit frucht. F. ἀσω. P. σεσιτάυκα.
Σίλυτος ἡ ὀν altilis e. à σιπάζω. Fut. ἰσω. P. σεσιπικα pinguefacio.
Σῖτ῾ ὁ proprie frumentum, per syn.gen. triticum, quod alio nomine vocatur πυρὸς ὁ. pl. σῖτα ὧν τὰ Act.7.12.

page.notes: Right margin notes are cut off and partly illegible; only fragments such as "menfura cibi", "Judith 5. v.1", "Act.27.27." and "tefracum" can be made out. Greek and Hebrew words are copied as far as they could be read; the German gloss "ein Dolch" and "messe mit frucht" are black letter. Doubtful Greek accents may be inaccurate.
